intended_object: The objects of the category of integral S-schemes with dominant rational S-maps between them: an integral scheme X together with a structure morphism X → S. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the `Category` instance defined just below, whose morphisms are dominant rational maps that are compatible with the structure morphisms.
explanation:
The structure holds three things: a scheme `toScheme`, a morphism `toBase : toScheme ⟶ S`, and a proof that `toScheme` is integral. In the literature, an object of the category of integral S-schemes with dominant rational maps is exactly this: an integral scheme X with a morphism X → S. As the docstring says, the structure morphism can be any morphism; it does not have to be dominant.

The type has to be separate from a full subcategory of `Over S`, because the library puts a different category structure on it: morphisms are dominant rational maps that commute with the structure maps up to rational equivalence. Mathlib has no category of integral schemes over S with rational maps, so there is no counterpart to cite.

Nothing is too narrow. S is an arbitrary scheme, and integrality is part of the notion itself: it is what makes dominant rational maps compose.
